description:
What happens when you build an operating system the way you build an application? In this GitHub Universe 2026 session, Jorge Castro from the CNCF uses Project Bluefin (projectbluefin.io) to demonstrate how container images, GitHub Actions, GitOps, and open source projects unite in a reproducible software supply chain. Discover where AI agents in CI/CD help update configurations and react to pipeline events while keeping builds traceable, reviewable, and secure. Learn practical patterns for integrating autonomous agents into DevOps workflows without replacing human oversight or essential controls. 

Speaker: 
Jorge Castro, Open Source Community Engineer and Developer Relations, CNCF 

Watch more videos from GitHub Universe 2026: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AArI948SDz8&list=PLENrlACZ7mnU

— CHAPTERS —

00:00 Welcome: agents in CI/CD
00:57 Project Bluefin: a Linux OS
02:42 AI transforms GitHub workflows
04:45 Agents need guidance: hive solution
07:43 Hive: orchestrating agent teams
title: What open source can teach us about agents in CI/CD

author: GitHub
description:
You meant to install requests, but you typed requests. In this Security in 60 Seconds short, Carlin Cherry explains typosquatting: attackers publish packages under names that resemble popular libraries, hoping a developer, a script, or even an AI assistant pulls in the wrong one. Once installed, malicious install scripts or code can run inside your environment. Before you install, verify the package, the publisher, the version, and what your build actually downloads.

Browse known malicious packages in the GitHub Advisory Database: https://github.com/advisories?query=type%3Amalware
Learn more about Dependabot malware alerts: https://gh.io/dependabot-malware
